title: Iowa's 3rd Congressional District election, 2026
description: Iowa's 3rd Congressional District is home to one of the most competitive U.S. House races in 2026, encompassing 21 counties in south-central Iowa including Des Moines, West Des Moines, Winterset, and Ottumwa. Incumbent Republican Rep. Zach Nunn is seeking a third term after narrowly winning re-election by four points in 2024, while the Democratic nominee is state Sen. Sarah Trone Garriott, a Lutheran minister and first-term state senator who emerged as the Democratic standard-bearer after state Rep. Jennifer Konfrst suspended her campaign in January 2026. Libertarian candidate Marco Battaglia is also running but faces ballot access challenges. The Cook Political Report rates the race as a toss-up, with the outcome likely to hinge on voter perceptions of economic conditions and President Donald Trump's approval in a district that narrowly backed Trump in 2024.
polling_note: Only one public poll with named candidates was found. Change Research conducted a survey showing Democratic candidates competitive but did not release specific named-candidate percentages for the matchup.

candidates.name: Zach Nunn
candidates.summary: Zach Nunn is a sixth-generation Iowan and combat veteran serving his second term as U.S. Representative for Iowa's 3rd Congressional District. He served nearly two decades in the U.S. Air Force as an airborne intelligence officer, deploying three times to the Middle East and flying over 700 combat hours, and later served as Director of Cybersecurity on the White House National Security Council. Nunn previously served in the Iowa House of Representatives and Iowa Senate before defeating incumbent Rep. Cindy Axne in 2022, and he sits on the House Financial Services, Agriculture, and Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party.

candidates.name: Sarah Trone Garriott
candidates.summary: Sarah Trone Garriott is an Iowa state senator, ordained Lutheran minister, and former nonprofit executive running to flip Iowa's 3rd Congressional District. She earned a B.A. from the College of Saint Scholastica, a Master of Theological Studies from Harvard Divinity School, and a Master of Divinity from the Lutheran School of Theology in Chicago. She serves as the ranking member on the Natural Resources and Environment Committee in the Iowa Senate and is the Democratic nominee after winning the June 2, 2026 primary unopposed after state Rep. Jennifer Konfrst suspended her campaign and endorsed her.

candidates.name: Marco Battaglia
candidates.summary: Marco Battaglia is a Libertarian candidate running for Iowa's 3rd Congressional District, a correctional officer at the Iowa Correctional Institution for Women in Mitchellville. He has run for office multiple times previously, including for Iowa Attorney General in 2018, lieutenant governor in 2022, and as a write-in candidate for this seat in 2024. His campaign focuses on eliminating tariffs, ending aggressive U.S. military action abroad, and streamlining immigration processing, but his ballot access is being challenged by Republican strategists and Rep. Zach Nunn's deputy chief of staff over signature sufficiency and name issues.
